The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #476a04;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #476a04;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #864f11;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #864f11;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #864f11;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e57;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e57;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e57;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8c3290;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c3290;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5150b1;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5150b1;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983f18;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983f18;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2d6d3e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2d6d3e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b5cb1;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b5cb1;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3740;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3740;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #666100;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7045a1;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7045a1;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #785800;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #785800;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #785800;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #476a04;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #17687b;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #17687b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #17687b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #666100;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276489;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276489;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276489;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933866;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933866;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933866;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
